name: Create an isometric voxel world
description: Build a small CSS 3D world with a clear sense of layers, materials, and composition. The output is an HTML artifact so the benchmark measures scene construction rather than SVG fluency.
prompt: Create a single self-contained file named voxel-world.html. Build a polished, static isometric voxel world using only inline HTML and CSS: a dark sky, a ground plane, at least nine visible cube/voxel elements, and three distinct depth layers marked with data-iso-layer values. Use CSS perspective and transform-style: preserve-3d, and give the scene a visible heading exactly "OpenEval Voxel World" plus a short legend. Make the composition feel intentional: vary the heights or materials of the voxels and include a foreground, middle, and background relationship. Do not use SVG, JavaScript, external assets, network requests, external stylesheets, images, fonts, or other files. This benchmark checks structure and source-level composition evidence; the rendered preview is a separate visual artifact, not a pixel-perfect verdict.

benchmark.intent: Whether the agent can turn a spatial art direction brief into a coherent layered CSS scene instead of satisfying a file-format checklist.
benchmark.deliverable: voxel-world.html with a previewable isometric scene

graders.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const s=fs.readFileSync('voxel-world.html','utf8'); const layers=[...s.matchAll(/data-iso-layer=['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]/g)].map(m=>m[1]); if(new Set(layers).size<3) process.exit(1); if((s.match(/class=['\"][^'\"]*\bvoxel\b/g)||[]).length<9) process.exit(1)"

graders.rubric: Review the bounded HTML/CSS artifact as source evidence for this brief: a coherent isometric voxel world with foreground/middle/background relationships, intentional material or height variation, a visible title and legend, and a composition that is more than repeated placeholder boxes. Reward concrete evidence in the source. Do not claim pixel-perfect visual quality from source alone.
